key_decisions: MPI-388 gets NO changelog entry. User's call and correct: MPI-356 shipped AFTER the 1.2.0 release, so the regression never reached a user. An in-cycle regression fixed in-cycle is not a release note.

Commit 638a308d (Krea 2 Enhance switched from the FLUX recipe to Cubric Prompt's krea-2 recipe) also gets NO entry, for a stronger reason found by the user: the Enhance button is only mounted when checkPromptEnhanceAvailable() succeeds (MpiPromptBox.js:1534-1555), Cubric Prompt is unreleased, so no 1.3 user ever sees the button and enhanceRecipe is unreachable. It is dev-only plumbing.

The MPI-388 drop fires POST-mount, not pre-mount. The box's live imageCount/videoCount are the only truthful read - a pre-mount read of state.promptMedia.gallery can disagree once slot-id mismatch and capacity/role eviction have had their say. It runs AFTER _wirePromptBox so the resulting operation-change updates the block's activeOperation instead of letting it drift, and it is deliberately NOT on the Reuse path, where a reused op is authoritative.

MPI-385 is NOT part of the MPI-387 umbrella - different subjects (Pod-only verification vs the Windows install). But they cannot run in parallel either: MPI-385 needs the app, the app binds port 3000, and the fix D staged boot binds the same port. Order is fix D boot -> free the port -> Pod session.

Four of MPI-385's five items are look-and-confirm on already-shipped, locally-verified fixes. Only MPI-380 (does the remote install path pick up a NEWLY ADDED engineAsset) is a real unknown, which is why it runs first.

THE SANDBOX EXPORTS ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, AND A STAGED PORTABLE EXE FAILS SILENTLY UNDER IT - exit 0, no window, no port bound, no stdout, nothing in any app.log. It reads exactly like a broken build and cost this session real time. The MPI-369 handler cannot catch it: in Node mode the destructured app/dialog are undefined, so reportFatal dies inside its own body. Tells: `--enable-logging` returns `bad option: --enable-logging` (a NODE message), and `--version` prints v24.14.0 instead of v41.1.1 - do NOT read a successful version print as 'the binary is fine', that IS the failure signature. `unset ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` in the SAME call as the launch; a PowerShell Start-Process inherits it from the bash process.

server.js:26 hardcodes port 3000. The dev app, a staged portable build, and any Pod session all contend for it. Check the OWNER before assuming it is free: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3000 -State Listen, then Get-CimInstance Win32_Process on OwningProcess and read the command line.

A verification build has two side effects on the tracked tree: pass --no-source-manifest or it overwrites resources/cubric/update-manifest.json, and a non-dry-run build needs docs/releases/.approved-<version>.json, a TRACKED file that `ls` does not show. Stage to a SHORT path - node given C:/tmp/x writes C:\tmp\x while bash /tmp is elsewhere.
